82.h: 78 - Khālid ibn al-Walīd al-Makhzūmī * (خ، م، د، س، ق)
82.t:
ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm ibn Yaqaẓah ibn Kaʿb.
The Sword of Allah the Exalted, the horseman of Islam, the lion of the battlefields, the master, the Imam (الإمام), the great commander, the leader of the mujāhidīn, Abū Sulaymān al-Qurashī, al-Makhzūmī, al-Makkī, and the son of the sister of the Mother (1) of the Believers Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith.
He emigrated as a Muslim in Ṣafar, in the year 8, then set out on campaign and was present at the expedition of Muʾtah. The three commanders appointed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were martyred: his client (المولى) Zayd, his cousin Jaʿfar of the two wings, and Ibn Rawāḥah. The army was left without a commander, so Khālid took command over them on the spot, took the banner, and charged the enemy, and victory came.
The Prophet ﷺ named him the Sword of Allah, saying: (Khālid is a sword that Allah has drawn against the polytheists).
He was present at the Conquest and at Ḥunayn, held command in the days of the Prophet ﷺ, dedicated his coats of mail and his armour in the path of Allah, fought the people of the apostasy and Musaylimah, campaigned in Iraq and prevailed, then crossed the Samāwah desert, so that he traversed the wasteland from the border of Iraq to the edge of Syria in five nights with an army that was with him. He was present at the wars of Syria, and there did not remain on his body the space of a hand-span without the ⟦1:366⟧ mark of the martyrs upon it.
His virtues are abundant. al-Ṣiddīq appointed him over all the commanders of the armies, and he besieged Damascus and conquered it, he and Abū ʿUbaydah.
He lived sixty years, killed a number of champions, and died on his bed: so may the eyes of the cowards find no rest.
He died in Ḥimṣ (1), in the year 21, and his shrine is at the gate of Ḥimṣ, with majesty upon it. ⟦1:367⟧
Narrating from him: ابن خالته عبد الله بن عباس، وقيس بن أبي حازم، والمقدام بن معدي كرب، وجبير بن نفير، وشقيق بن سلمة، وآخرون.
He has few hadiths.
مسلم: من طريق ابن شهاب، عن أبي أمامة بن سهل، أن ابن عباس أخبره، أن خالد بن الوليد - الذي كان يقال له: سيف الله - أخبره:
That he went in to his maternal aunt Maymūnah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found with her a roasted lizard, which her sister Ḥufaydah bint al-Ḥārith had brought from Najd. She offered it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he withdrew his hand.
Khālid said: Is it forbidden, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: (No, but it was not found in the land of my people, so I find that I have an aversion to it).
So I drew it towards me (1) and ate it, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was watching, and he did not forbid me (2).
هشام بن حسان: عن حفصة بنت سيرين، عن أبي العالية:
That Khālid ibn al-Walīd said: O Messenger of Allah! A plotter from among the jinn is plotting against me.
He said: (Say: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can transgress, from the evil of what He has scattered in the earth and what comes out ⟦1:368⟧ of it, from the evil of what ascends into the sky and what descends from it, and from the evil of every night-visitor except a night-visitor (1) who comes with good, O Most Merciful).
So I did it, and Allah removed him from me (2).
وعن حيان بن أبي جبلة، عن عمرو بن العاص، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not regard anyone as equal to me and Khālid in his warfare from the time we embraced Islam (3).
يونس بن أبي إسحاق: عن العيزار بن حريث:
That Khālid ibn al-Walīd came to al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā and said:
O (ʿUzz), your denial, not your glorification! ... I have seen that Allah has humiliated you
وروى: زكريا بن أبي زائدة، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي: that Khālid said the like of it.
Qatādah said: Khālid walked up to al-ʿUzzā and broke her nose with the axe.
وروى: سفيان بن حسين، عن قتادة:
That the Prophet ﷺ sent Khālid to al-ʿUzzā, which belonged to Hawāzin, and its custodians were Banū Sulaym. He said: (Go, for a woman will come out against you, ⟦1:369⟧ intensely black, long-haired, with huge breasts, short).
They said, urging her on:
O (ʿUzz), charge with a charge that has no equal (1) ... at Khālid; throw off the veil and tuck up your garment
For if you do not kill the man Khālid ... you will bear a swift sin and fall short
So Khālid charged at her and killed her, and said: al-ʿUzzā is gone, and there will be no al-ʿUzzā after today (2).
الزهري: عن عبد الرحمن بن أزهر:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn making his way through the people, asking for Khālid's camp. He was directed to it, and he looked at his wound, and I think that he blew upon it (3).
Ibn ʿUmar said: The Prophet ﷺ sent Khālid to Banū Jadhīmah, and he killed and took captives.
The Prophet ﷺ raised his hands and said: (O Allah, I declare myself innocent before You of what Khālid has done), twice (4).
الواقدي: عن رجل، عن إياس بن سلمة، عن أبيه، قال:
When Khālid came back after what he had done to Banū Jadhīmah, Ibn ʿAwf reproached him for what he had done and said:
You acted by the custom of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية); you killed them in retaliation for your uncle al-Fākih, may Allah fight you. ⟦1:370⟧
He said: ʿUmar also reproached him, and Khālid said: I took them for the killing of your father.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: You lied. I killed my father's killer with my own hand, and even had I not killed him, you would be killing a Muslim people for my father of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية).
He said: And who told you that they had become Muslims?
He said: The people of the raiding party, all of them.
He said: The messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me telling me to raid them, so I raided.
He said: You have lied against the Messenger of Allah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from Khālid, became angry, and said: (O Khālid! Leave my companions to me; whenever a man's intimate is wounded, the man himself is wounded (1)).
الواقدي: حدثنا يحيى بن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة، عن أهله، عن أبي قتادة، قال:
When Khālid called out before dawn: Whoever has a captive with him, let him finish him off, I released my captive and said to Khālid:
Fear Allah, for you will die, and these are a Muslim people.
He said: You have no knowledge of these people.
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) includes al-Wāqidī; and Khālid had his independent legal reasoning (الاجتهاد), and for that reason the Prophet ﷺ did not demand of him their blood-money (الدية).
الواقدي: حدثنا يوسف بن يعقوب بن عتبة، عن عثمان الأخنسي، عن عبد الملك بن أبي بكر، قال:
The Prophet ﷺ sent Khālid to al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb as a commander and a summoner.
He went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Farewell Pilgrimage, and when he shaved his head, he gave him his forelock, which was placed in the front of Khālid's cap, and he never met an enemy without routing them (2).
And someone who washed him in Ḥimṣ and looked at what was beneath his clothes informed me, saying:
There is no sound spot on him; it is all between a blow of a sword, a thrust of a spear, or a shot of an arrow. ⟦1:371⟧
الوليد بن مسلم: حدثنا وحشي بن حرب، عن أبيه، عن جده وحشي:
That Abū Bakr tied the banner for Khālid to fight the people of the apostasy, and said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Khālid ibn al-Walīd is one of the swords of Allah, which Allah has drawn against the disbelievers and the hypocrites).
Aḥmad narrated it in (his Musnad (1)).
هشام بن عروة: عن أبيه، قال:
There was apostasy among Banū Sulaym, so Abū Bakr sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to them. He gathered men of theirs in enclosures, then burned them.
ʿUmar said to Abū Bakr: Do you leave alone a man who punishes with the punishment of Allah?
He said: By Allah, I will not sheathe (2) a sword that Allah has drawn against His enemy.
Then he gave him his orders, and he went on to Musaylimah (3).
ضمرة بن ربيعة: أخبرني السيباني (4) ، عن أبي العجماء - but in fact he is Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ - السلمي، قال:
It was said to ʿUmar: If only you would appoint a successor, O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين)!
He said: Had I lived to see Abū ʿUbaydah and then appointed him, and then come before my Lord and He had said to me: Why did you make him your successor?
I would have said: I heard Your servant and Your intimate friend say: (Every community has a trustee, and the trustee of this community is Abū ʿUbaydah).
And had I lived to see Khālid ibn al-Walīd and then appointed him, and come before my Lord, I would have said:
I heard Your servant and Your intimate friend say: (Khālid is one of the swords of Allah, which Allah has drawn against ⟦1:372⟧ the polytheists) (1).
al-Shāshī (2) also narrated it in (his Musnad).
Aḥmad in (al-Musnad): حدثنا حسين الجعفي، عن زائدة، عن عبد الملك بن عمير، قال:
ʿUmar appointed Abū ʿUbaydah over Syria and dismissed Khālid.
Abū ʿUbaydah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Khālid is one of the swords of Allah; what an excellent young man of the clan he is (3)).
حميد بن هلال: عن أنس:
The Prophet ﷺ announced the death of the commanders (4) on the day of Muʾtah, and said: (They were all struck down; then after them one of the swords of Allah took the banner: Khālid).
And he began telling the people, while his eyes were shedding tears (5).
إسماعيل بن أبي خالد: عن قيس: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Khālid is but a sword ⟦1:373⟧ of the swords of Allah, which He has poured out upon the disbelievers (1)).
أبو إسماعيل المؤدب: عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن الشعبي، عن ابن أبي أوفى، as raised (المرفوع), with its meaning.
It has come by several routes from Abū Hurayrah, similarly.
أبو المسكين الطائي: حدثنا عمران بن زحر، حدثني حميد بن منيب، قال جدي أوس:
No one was more hostile to the Arabs than Hurmuz. When we had finished with Musaylimah, we came to the region of Basra and met Hurmuz at Kāẓimah. Khālid fought him in single combat and killed him, and al-Ṣiddīq awarded him his spoils. His cap reached a hundred thousand dirhams; the Persians, for anyone of great standing among them, would make his cap worth a hundred thousand.
Abū Wāʾil said: Khālid wrote to the Persians:
I have with me troops who love death as the Persians love wine.
هشيم: حدثنا عبد الحميد بن جعفر، عن أبيه:
That Khālid ibn al-Walīd lost a cap of his on the day of al-Yarmūk, and said: Look for it.
They did not find it; then it was found, and behold, it was a worn-out cap.
Khālid said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿumrah and shaved his head, and the people rushed for his hair, but I beat them to his forelock and put it in this cap. I have never been present at a battle while it was ⟦1:374⟧ with me without being granted victory (1).
ابن وهب: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد، عن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث، أخبرني الثقة:
That on the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shaved, the people rushed for his hair, but Khālid beat them to his forelock and put it in his cap (2).
ابن أبي خالد: عن قيس، سمعت خالدا يقول:
I saw myself on the day of Muʾtah: nine swords broke in my hand, and only a broad Yemeni blade held firm in my hand (3).
ابن عيينة: عن ابن أبي خالد، عن مولى لآل خالد بن الوليد:
That Khālid said: There is no night on which a bride I love is brought to me that is dearer to me than a night of severe cold and heavy frost, in a raiding party that falls upon the enemy at dawn (4).
يونس بن أبي إسحاق: عن العيزار بن حريث، قال:
Khālid said: I do not know from which of my two days I would flee: a day on which Allah wished to give me martyrdom, or a day on which Allah wished to give me honour.
Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim said: I heard Khālid say: Jihad kept me from much of ⟦1:375⟧ the recitation of the Qurʾān (1). And I saw him when poison was brought to him. They said: What is this?
They said: Poison.
He said: In the name of Allah, and drank it.
I say: This, by Allah, is the miracle of grace, and this is courage.
يونس بن أبي إسحاق: عن أبي السفر، قال:
Khālid ibn al-Walīd stopped at al-Ḥīrah with the mother of Banū al-Marāzibah. They said: Beware of poison; do not let the non-Arabs make you drink it.
He said: Bring it to me.
It was brought to him, and he plunged into it and said: In the name of Allah, and it did not harm him (2).
أبو بكر بن عياش: عن الأعمش، عن خيثمة، قال:
A man with a skin of wine was brought to Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and he said:
O Allah, make it honey, and it became honey (3).
رواه: يحيى بن آدم، عن أبي بكر، and he said: vinegar, instead of honey, and this is more likely.
ويرويه: عطاء بن السائب، عن محارب بن دثار as mursal (مرسل).
ابن أبي خالد: عن قيس، قال:
Khālid ibn al-Walīd divorced a woman, and they spoke to him about it. He said:
No misfortune befell her while with me, nor any trial, nor any illness, and that made me suspicious of her (4).
المدائني: عن ابن أبي ذئب، عن الزهري، عن سالم، عن أبيه، قال:
Abū Qatādah came to Abū Bakr and told him of the killing of Mālik ibn Nuwayrah and his companions. He was distressed, ⟦1:376⟧ and wrote to Khālid, who came to him.
Abū Bakr said: Can you say more than that he made an interpretation and erred?
Then he sent him back, paid the blood-money (الدية) for Mālik, and returned the captives and the property (1).
From Ibn Isḥāq, who said:
Khālid went in to Abū Bakr, informed him, and apologised, and he excused him.
Sayf said in (al-Riddah): عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، قال:
Some people of the raiding party testified that they had given the call to prayer, made the iqāmah, and prayed, and that they had done likewise.
Others testified to the contrary, so they were killed.
His brother Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah came, appealing to al-Ṣiddīq for his blood and demanding the captives, and he wrote ordering that the captives be returned.
ʿUmar pressed him to dismiss Khālid, and said: There is recklessness in his sword.
He said: No, O ʿUmar; I would not sheathe (2) a sword that Allah has drawn against the disbelievers (3).
سيف: عن ابن إسحاق، عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير، وغيره:
That Khālid sent out the raiding parties, and Mālik was brought to him.
People differed in what they said about them and about their Islam. Umm Tamīm came with her face uncovered and threw herself upon Mālik; she was the most beautiful of people.
He said to her: Get away from me, for, by Allah, you have killed me.
Khālid gave the order concerning them, and their necks were struck. Abū Qatādah stood and implored him by Allah concerning them, but he paid no attention to him.
So Abū Qatādah mounted his horse, caught up with Abū Bakr, and swore: I will not march in an army that is under the banner of Khālid. And he said:
He abandoned my word and took the testimony of the Bedouins whom the spoils had seduced (4). ⟦1:377⟧
ابن سعد: أنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثني عتبة بن جبيرة، عن عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة.
قال: وحدثني محمد بن عبد الله، عن الزهري.
وحدثنا أسامة بن زيد، عن الزهري، عن حنظلة بن علي الأسلمي, in the account of the apostasy:
Khālid fell upon them and killed Mālik; then he fell upon the people of Buzākhah (1) and burned them, because a vile saying of theirs had reached him: they had reviled the Prophet ﷺ. Then he went on to al-Yamāmah and killed Musaylimah.
Until he said: Khālid came to Medina with the captives, and with him were seventeen of the delegation of Banū Ḥanīfah. He entered the mosque wearing a tunic stained with the rust of iron, girded with the sword, with arrows in his turban.
He passed by ʿUmar, who did not speak to him, and went in to Abū Bakr, and saw from him everything he could wish. ʿUmar learned of it and held back.
ʿUmar was angry with him only because he had killed Mālik ibn Nuwayrah and married his wife.
Juwayriyah ibn Asmāʾ said:
Khālid ibn al-Walīd was among the most far-sighted of people. He saw a rider, and behold, he had come with news of the death of al-Ṣiddīq and of Khālid's dismissal.
Ibn ʿAwn said: ʿUmar took office and said:
I shall remove (2) Khālid, so that he may know that Allah alone gives victory to His religion.
Meaning: without Khālid.
وقال هشام بن عروة: عن أبيه، قال:
When ʿUmar became caliph, he wrote to Abū ʿUbaydah: I have appointed you, and I have dismissed Khālid.
Khalīfah said: ʿUmar appointed Abū ʿUbaydah over Syria, and he appointed Yazīd over Palestine, Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah over Jordan, Khālid ibn al-Walīd over Damascus, and Ḥabīb ibn ⟦1:378⟧ Maslamah over Ḥimṣ.
الزبير بن بكار: حدثني محمد بن مسلمة، عن مالك، قال:
ʿUmar said to Abū Bakr: Write to Khālid that he is not to give away a sheep or a camel except by your order.
So Abū Bakr wrote that.
He said: Khālid wrote to him: Either you leave me to my post, or else, see to your post yourself.
ʿUmar advised dismissing him, and he said: And who will suffice in his place?
ʿUmar said: I.
He said: Then you.
Mālik said: Zayd ibn Aslam said: ʿUmar made his preparations, until the riding camels were made to kneel in the courtyard.
The time for setting out came, and a group went to Abū Bakr and said:
What is the matter with you! You send ʿUmar out of Medina when you are in need of him, and you have dismissed Khālid when he has sufficed you?
He said: So what should I do?
They said: Insist that ʿUmar stay, and write to Khālid so that he remains at his post. And he did so (1).
هشام بن سعد: عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه:
ʿUmar said to Abū Bakr: Will you leave Khālid in Syria spending the wealth of Allah?
He said: When Abū Bakr died, Aslam said:
I heard ʿUmar say: I would be lying to Allah if I had ordered Abū Bakr to do something that I myself do not do.
So he wrote to Khālid, and Khālid wrote to him: I have no need of your post.
So he appointed Abū ʿUbaydah.
الحارث بن يزيد: عن علي بن رباح، عن ناشرة اليزني:
I heard ʿUmar at al-Jābiyah apologising for the dismissal of Khālid. He said: And I appointed Abū ʿUbaydah.
Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah (2) said: By Allah, you have not given a valid excuse. You have removed a governor whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed, and lowered a banner that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised.
He said: You are a close relative, young in age, angered on behalf of your cousin (3). ⟦1:379⟧
From the book of Sayf, from his men, who said:
Nothing of his governors' doings was hidden from ʿUmar. Khālid had given al-Ashʿath a gift of ten thousand.
So he summoned the courier and wrote to Abū ʿUbaydah:
That you stand Khālid up, tie him with his turban, and remove his cap until he informs you from where he gave al-Ashʿath the gift: was it from the wealth of Allah or from his own wealth? If he claims it is from booty he obtained, then he has confessed to embezzlement; and if he claims it is from his own wealth, then he has been extravagant. Dismiss him in any case, and take over his post yourself.
He did that. Khālid came to ʿUmar and complained of him, and said:
I have complained of you to the Muslims, and by Allah, O ʿUmar, you have not treated me fairly in my affair.
ʿUmar said: Where does this wealth come from?
He said: From the spoils and the shares. Whatever exceeds sixty thousand is yours; let his goods be valued.
He said: Twenty thousand came out against him, and he put it into the treasury.
Then he said: O Khālid! By Allah, you are honoured by me and you are dear to me, and you will not reproach me after today about anything (1).
وعن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه:
ʿUmar dismissed Khālid, and Abū ʿUbaydah did not inform him until he learned it from others.
He said: May Allah have mercy on you! What made you not inform me?
He said: I disliked to alarm you.
جويرية بن أسماء: عن نافع، قال:
Khālid came from Syria with arrows in his turban smeared with blood, and ʿUmar forbade him.
الأصمعي: عن ابن عون، عن ابن سيرين:
That Khālid ibn al-Walīd came in wearing a silk shirt.
ʿUmar said: What is this?
He said: What harm is there in it? Ibn ʿAwf has worn it (2). ⟦1:380⟧
He said: And you are like him?! I adjure everyone in the house to take a piece of it each. So they tore it to pieces.
روى عاصم بن بهدلة: عن أبي وائل, I think he said:
When death came to Khālid, he said:
I sought death in its likely places, but it was decreed for me only to die on my bed. And there is nothing among my deeds more hopeful to me, after tawḥīd, than a night I spent shielded, with the sky pouring rain upon me, as we waited for the dawn so that we could raid the disbelievers.
Then he said: When I die, look to my weapons and my horse, and make them equipment in the path of Allah.
When he died, ʿUmar went out at his funeral and mentioned his saying:
There is no blame on the women of the family of al-Walīd if they shed their tears over Khālid, so long as there is no naqʿ or laqlaqah (1).
al-Naqʿ: dust on the heads.
And al-laqlaqah: wailing.
And it is narrated with a worthless chain of transmission (الإسناد) that ʿUmar went out at the funeral of Khālid in Medina, and behold, his mother was lamenting him and saying:
You were better than a million of the peo ... ple when the faces of men were cast down ⟦1:381⟧
ʿUmar said: She has spoken the truth; he was indeed like that (1).
الواقدي: حدثنا عمرو بن (2) عبد الله بن عنبسة:
I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Dībāj say:
Khālid remained with Abū ʿUbaydah until Abū ʿUbaydah died and appointed ʿIyāḍ ibn Ghanm as his successor.
Khālid remained with ʿIyāḍ until he died; then Khālid withdrew to Ḥimṣ and stayed there. He dedicated horses and weapons, and remained on frontier garrison duty (الرباط) in Ḥimṣ until death came upon him.
Abū al-Dardāʾ visited him in his illness, and he mentioned to him: that his horses that were dedicated at the frontier were being fed from my wealth, and my house in Medina is a charity, and I had made ʿUmar a witness to it. By Allah, O Abū al-Dardāʾ, if ʿUmar dies you will see things you will disapprove of.
وروى: إسحاق بن يحيى بن طلحة، عن عمه موسى، قال:
I went out with my father Ṭalḥah to Mecca with ʿUmar, and while we were unloading our mounts, news came of the death of Khālid.
ʿUmar cried out: O Abū Muḥammad! O Ṭalḥah! Abū Sulaymān has perished; Khālid ibn al-Walīd has perished.
Ṭalḥah said:
Let me not find you, after death, mourning me ... when in my life you gave me no provision (3)
From Abū al-Zinād: that when death came to Khālid ibn al-Walīd, he wept and said:
I have met such-and-such a number of battles, and there is not a hand-span on my body without a blow of a sword or a shot of an arrow in it, and here I am dying on my bed a natural death, as the donkey dies (4). So may the eyes of the cowards find no rest.
Muṣʿab ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: Khālid remained in Syria until ʿUmar dismissed him, and he died in Syria, and ʿUmar took charge of his will. ⟦1:382⟧
Ibn Abī al-Zinād said: He died in Ḥimṣ, in the year 21. Before that he had come performing ʿumrah, and returned.
الواقدي: حدثنا عمر بن عبد الله بن رياح، عن خالد بن رياح، سمع ثعلبة بن أبي مالك يقول:
I saw ʿUmar at Qubāʾ, and behold, there were pilgrims from Syria.
He said: Who are these people?
They said: From Yemen, of those who settled in Ḥimṣ; and on the day we set out from it Khālid ibn al-Walīd died.
ʿUmar said "To Allah we belong and to Him we return" again and again, lowered his head, and prayed much for mercy upon him, and said:
He was, by Allah, a barrier against the enemy's throat, of blessed leadership.
ʿAlī said to him: Then why did you dismiss him?!
He said: I dismissed him for his giving wealth to people of rank and to those with eloquent tongues.
He said: You could have removed him from the wealth and left him over the army.
He said: He would not have been satisfied.
He said: Then why did you not test him (1)?
وروى: جويرية، عن نافع، قال:
When Khālid died, he left nothing but his horse, his weapons, and his slave.
ʿUmar said: May Allah have mercy on Abū Sulaymān; he was as we had thought of him (2).
الأعمش: عن أبي وائل، قال:
The women of Banū al-Mughīrah gathered in Khālid's house weeping for him.
ʿUmar said: There is no blame on them if they shed their tears, so long as there is no naqʿ or laqlaqah (3).
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir, and Abū ʿUbayd said:
Khālid died in Ḥimṣ, in the year 21.
Duḥaym said: He died in Medina. ⟦1:383⟧
I say: the correct view is that he died in Ḥimṣ, and he has a shrine that is visited.
He has in (the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين)): two hadiths, and in (the Musnad of Baqī): seventy-one.
